source: On convergence of the Flint Hills series (arXiv:1104.5100)
missing_details: the explicit formula of the series: ∑_{n=1}^∞ 1/(n^3 (sin n)^2)
the domain of summation (n runs over positive integers)
that the sine function is evaluated in radians
that it is unknown whether the series converges or diverges
refined_question: Determine whether the infinite series \(S=\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{n^3(\sin n)^2}\), where \(n\) ranges over the positive integers and the sine function uses radian measure, converges to a finite limit.
justification: The series in question is defined as \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty1/(n^3\sin^2n)\) and its convergence remains an open problem ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.5100)). The problem name indicates that one must decide convergence of a specific series, but does not state the series’ formula, index domain, or measurement conventions, all of which are necessary for a precise, standalone research question.
